sources.finding: GPT-6.1 Sol is recommended for complex coding and agentic workflows when available; Astra remains appropriate for the hardest work and Luna for repeatable tasks.
GPT-6.1 Sol is a starting point for demanding agents; custom model and effort pins override dispatch values.
API efforts are low, medium, high, xhigh and max; none and minimal are unsupported. Tool calling requires Responses. API effort controls do not define Codex Ultra.
The family-wide prompting examples explicitly describe Astra behavior and require evaluation with the chosen model/workload. No new Sol-specific instruction rewrite is established.
GPT-6.1 Sol released September 29. Standard API input/output rates match GPT-6 Sol; cached input costs less. This does not prove total task cost or Codex credit savings.

runtime_evidence: Current desktop tool metadata exposes gpt-6.1-sol with low, medium, high, xhigh, max and ultra. This is a configuration capability snapshot, not served identity or task-quality proof.
decision: User selected official documentation plus bounded smoke and authorized managed installed updates; preserve existing efforts and the tiered Astra/Luna routing.
prompting_decision: Preserve existing behavioral instruction text. Update only active model/capability/evidence metadata.
